slides.text: GM just spent two years testing one rollout. You should too.
slides.voiceover_text: General Motors took two years to roll out one piece of tech across the company. Small firms sign annual contracts after a thirty minute demo. Here's the test to do instead.

slides.text: Define success in hours saved on a real task
slides.voiceover_text: One. Define success before you start. Not does it work. Does it save X hours a week on Y task. Specific number. Specific job.

slides.text: Test with real work, not the polished demo
slides.voiceover_text: Two. Test with real work. Actual enquiries. Actual data. Edge cases. Demos are built to win. Real work tells the truth.
Three. Smallest contract possible. Month to month beats annual until you've got ninety days of real data. Commit fast, regret slowly.

slides.text: Define success. Test real. Stay short.
slides.voiceover_text: Define success. Test on real work. Stay on a short contract. That's how the big firms decide. Small firms should too.
